## Random Forest Models and Class Imbalance

This script evaluates three approaches to using Random Forest models for imbalanced datasets: Basic Random Forest, Weighted Random Forest, and Random Forest with SMOTE.

```r
# Load required libraries
library(randomForest)
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(tidyverse)
library(mltools)

# Ensure y is a factor for classification
y_train <- as.factor(y_train)
y_test <- as.factor(y_test)

# 1. Basic Random Forest Model
# Train the Random Forest model
set.seed(42)
rf_model <- randomForest(x = X_train, y = y_train, ntree = 100, mtry = sqrt(ncol(X_train)), importance = TRUE)

# Predict on the test set
y_pred <- predict(rf_model, X_test)
y_pred_proba <- predict(rf_model, X_test, type = "prob")[, 2]

# Evaluate model performance
conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(y_pred, y_test)
print("Basic Random Forest - Confusion Matrix:")
print(conf_matrix)

roc_curve <- roc(as.numeric(y_test) - 1, as.numeric(y_pred_proba))
auc_value <- auc(roc_curve)
print(paste("Basic Random Forest - AUC:", auc_value))

# Plot Feature Importance
print("Basic Random Forest - Feature Importance:")
varImpPlot(rf_model)

# 2. Random Forest with Weighted Classes
# Define class weights for imbalanced data
class_weights <- c("0" = 1, "1" = 70)

# Train the weighted Random Forest model
set.seed(42)
rf_model_weighted <- randomForest(x = X_train, y = y_train, ntree = 100, mtry = sqrt(ncol(X_train)), 
                                  importance = TRUE, classwt = class_weights)

# Predict on the test set
y_pred_weighted <- predict(rf_model_weighted, X_test)
y_pred_proba_weighted <- predict(rf_model_weighted, X_test, type = "prob")[, 2]

# Evaluate model performance
conf_matrix_weighted <- confusionMatrix(y_pred_weighted, y_test)
print("Weighted Random Forest - Confusion Matrix:")
print(conf_matrix_weighted)

roc_curve_weighted <- roc(as.numeric(y_test) - 1, as.numeric(y_pred_proba_weighted))
auc_value_weighted <- auc(roc_curve_weighted)
print(paste("Weighted Random Forest - AUC:", auc_value_weighted))

# Plot Feature Importance
print("Weighted Random Forest - Feature Importance:")
varImpPlot(rf_model_weighted)

# 3. Random Forest with SMOTE
# Combine X_train and y_train into a single data frame for SMOTE
train_data <- cbind(X_train, TARGET = y_train)

# Apply SMOTE to balance the classes in the training set
set.seed(42)
smote_result <- SMOTE(train_data[,-ncol(train_data)], train_data$TARGET, K = 5, dup_size = 2)
train_balanced <- smote_result$data

# Convert SMOTE results to appropriate format
train_balanced$TARGET <- as.factor(ifelse(train_balanced$class == "1", 1, 0))
train_balanced <- train_balanced %>% select(-class)

# Separate X_train and y_train after SMOTE
X_train_balanced <- train_balanced %>% select(-TARGET)
y_train_balanced <- train_balanced$TARGET

# Train the SMOTE-balanced Random Forest model with class weights
set.seed(42)
rf_model_smote <- randomForest(x = X_train_balanced, y = y_train_balanced, ntree = 100, 
                               mtry = sqrt(ncol(X_train_balanced)), importance = TRUE, classwt = class_weights)

# Predict on the test set
y_pred_smote <- predict(rf_model_smote, X_test)
y_pred_proba_smote <- predict(rf_model_smote, X_test, type = "prob")[, 2]

# Evaluate model performance
conf_matrix_smote <- confusionMatrix(y_pred_smote, y_test)
print("SMOTE Random Forest - Confusion Matrix:")
print(conf_matrix_smote)

roc_curve_smote <- roc(as.numeric(y_test) - 1, as.numeric(y_pred_proba_smote))
auc_value_smote <- auc(roc_curve_smote)
print(paste("SMOTE Random Forest - AUC:", auc_value_smote))

# Plot Feature Importance
print("SMOTE Random Forest - Feature Importance:")
varImpPlot(rf_model_smote)
